content:
Avery Johnson: Anyone have (or can we get) a one-slide “why Redwood” summary pulled from the case studies? Need something we can drop into outbound + late-stage decks. Not the full story pages—just the punchy proof points + what to say.

Stephanie Nguyen: +1. Sales is hacking this together deal-by-deal. Would love a standard slide w/ approved language and a metrics disclaimer.

Camila Reyes: Yep, this is on our enablement list. We can pull from Northwind draft + the approved pillars doc. @Soojin Lee can you take first pass on copy? @Ethan Wallace can you sanity check it’s consistent with the case study narratives?

Soojin Lee: On it. Quick q: do you want this as (a) generic “Why Redwood Inference” (no customer names) or (b) “Proof from customers” w/ small callouts (Northwind/Helios/Polaris) where permitted?

Avery Johnson: Ideally both, but if we pick one: generic slide w/ 3–4 bullets + 1–2 proof callouts. We can swap logos depending on approval status.

Ethan Wallace: Current state:
- Northwind: public story basically ready, quotes + architecture diagram approved pending final legal window.
- Helios: likely needs anonymized language + metric ranges only.
- Polaris: ok for “time-to-value/devex” angle, but metrics are still in review.
So for now, maybe one “Northwind proof” callout + “others available on request”.

Markus Klein: For the technical bulleting, we should keep it to what we can back up:
- predictable throughput on Dedicated (reserved GPUs)
- reliability via routing/fallback policies
- cost controls via batching/caching + Optimize recommendations
Avoid: “X% faster than competitor” unless we’ve got the metrics sheet signed.

Simran Kaur: +1. Also let’s avoid naming specific kernel tricks on sales slides. We can say “high-throughput runtime w/ continuous batching + KV cache management” in plain terms.

Tyler Benson: When you say “one-slide,” do you want in our standard deck theme? If yes I can drop it into the Sales Master template and share a link.

Avery Johnson: Standard theme please. Also add a tiny footer disclaimer re: metrics being customer-reported / varies by workload.

Soojin Lee: Draft structure proposal:
Header: “Why Redwood Inference (what customers buy)”
Bullets (approved pillars):
1) Performance economics: lower $/1M tokens w/ batching/caching + right-sized model/quant profiles
2) Reliability: SLO-oriented serving w/ automated fallbacks + graceful degradation
3) Deployment flexibility: Hosted → Dedicated → Private (VPC/on-prem) w/ consistent API + rollouts
4) Operational tooling: Console visibility (token cost/latency) + eval hooks to prevent regressions
Proof box (right side): Northwind callout w/ 1 quote + 2 metrics (if we can do ranges)
CTA: “Ask us for references / case studies by deployment type”

Isabelle Laurent: If we’re putting “references available,” we should include the internal tag language so reps know how to request + we can track utilization (for reporting). Maybe a tiny note in speaker notes: “Log reference usage on deal: Reference Used = Yes; Asset = Why Redwood slide / Case Study”.

Camila Reyes: Love it. For this slide we can keep the tracking instruction in speaker notes (not visible) so we don’t clutter.

Soojin Lee: Copy draft (v0) below—tell me what needs tightening:
“Why teams choose Redwood for production LLM inference
• Predictable performance at scale: optimized serving runtime with workload-aware batching + KV cache management
• Reliability by design: policy-based routing + automatic fallback keeps apps online when capacity is constrained
• Deploy anywhere: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, or Private (VPC/on‑prem) with the same interface + rollout controls
• Operate with confidence: per-route cost/latency visibility and eval-driven monitoring to prevent quality regressions”
Proof callout:
“Northwind Commerce (Dedicated)
‘We hit our latency targets without losing cost control.’ — VP Engineering
Results: p95 latency improved (range) + spend per 1M tokens reduced (range) after tuning batching/caching”
Footer: “Results vary by model, workload, and measurement method. Metrics shown are customer-reported and/or validated during deployment.”

Markus Klein: Looks good. Suggest change “optimized serving runtime” → “high-throughput serving runtime” (less ‘sounds like magic’) and replace “keeps apps online” w/ “reduces downtime risk” (legal tends to prefer that).

Ethan Wallace: Also quote should be exact wording from approved doc. If we’re not 100% sure yet, swap in a placeholder: “Customer quote available on request (approved references)” until Avery’s thread closes.

Tyler Benson: I can implement the layout now w/ placeholder quote + metric ranges stubbed as “XX–YY%” and we can update once legal signs off. Where should I pull the disclaimer language from—do we have a standard?

Camila Reyes: Use the metrics disclaimer from the docs PR (the one on the case study page). Keep it short.

Soojin Lee: I’ll DM you the exact disclaimer sentence. @Tyler Benson please share link here once slide is in the master template.

Tyler Benson: Done. Slide added to Sales Master Deck under “Customer Proof / Case Studies” section. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/redwood-sales-master (slide 14). Speaker notes include the HubSpot logging reminder.

Avery Johnson: Pulled it—this is exactly what I needed. Will test in two late-stage calls tomorrow. If anyone wants edits based on prospect questions, drop them here.

Stephanie Nguyen: :thumbsup: Thank you. Next ask: once Helios is cleared (anonymized), can we do a variant slide for security/compliance-heavy buyers?

Camila Reyes: Yep. We’ll create a “Private / regulated workloads” variant once Helios language is finalized. Tracking as follow-up item in enablement.
